summary: Owner-authored spec-quality issue with clear desired outcomes and design forks explicitly delegated; confirmed the branch-protection rework loop is a genuine, still-open bug on main (mapMergeState drops mergeable_state, poller re-promotes /approve unbounded). No blocking questions.

acceptance_criteria: A merge the host will not complete (branch protection / required review / not-actually-mergeable) never routes the task into execution/implement rework.
An authorized /approve that branch protection will not honor is surfaced/escalated to the owner with an actionable reason, not silently re-promoted every poll or looped.

The pr_ready_to_merge / /approve-promotion re-entry path is bounded or gated so a promotion that structurally cannot complete cannot loop unbounded (closing the gap max_blocker_reentries does not cover).

Readiness is decided using the host's real 'will this merge?' signal (e.g. GitHub mergeable_state/mergeStateStatus and/or reviewDecision), not just the boolean mergeable, so 'mergeable shape but blocked by protection' is distinguished from 'mergeable and the host will merge'.
A genuinely approved + green + host-will-merge PR still merges automatically with no behavior change (regression preserved).
Host-specific merge-blocked detection lives in the git-hosting plugin behind the adapter contract; the wait/escalate/route policy lives in Core so a second hosting plugin inherits the safety.
A genuine merge conflict (base moved, no longer mergeable) still routes to execution rework as today — the new 'blocked merge never reworks' rule does not swallow real conflicts.

The change is covered by unit tests for the blocked-merge routing (poller promotion + auto-merge readiness/failure classification) and the project's gates pass (typecheck, lint, tests). The CI non-final debounce (issue #46) is out of scope.
